title: Sam Parr: audience vs community, pricing high, and building brand before spreadsheets
summary: Sam Parr explains why he sold The Hustle to HubSpot and what he changed building Hampton. He covers prioritizing brand over finance early, charging more, launching businesses to an audience, and the real difference between an audience and a community.

principles.text: Ignore admin early; brand and product are the parts you can't fix later.
principles.quote: the brand stuff and like the making the product that stuff you can't figure out later you got to nail that

principles.text: Get a first sale before spending on domains or legal setup.
principles.quote: go and get a sale or collect some type of money for your for your product before you even have a domain name

principles.text: An audience is one-to-many; a community is many-to-many and grows without you.
principles.quote: an audience is one to many it's Nick posting videos it's Sam posting a podcast a community is many to many

principles.text: First-time founders underinvest in marketing and distribution, and underprice.
principles.quote: a lot of first-time entrepreneurs they care about like product and stuff like that which is important but not enough about marketing and distribution so like getting eyeballs and customers

principles.text: Price high enough to fund a good service and acquire customers; go upmarket.
principles.quote: in order to make the service good I had to charge a lot of money

principles.text: Build an audience, then launch real businesses to it instead of just selling ads.
principles.quote: instead I think you should launch businesses to your audience and I think that that's a really interesting move
